title: C# - `StringExtensions` improvements

milestone.title: 4.x
milestone.description: Issues and pull requests slated for an undetermined Godot 4 release.

body:
This pull request makes a number of improvements (bug fixes, performance improvements, simplicity/clarity improvements) I found to `StringExtensions` in C#.

- Replaced calls `RFind(string)` with constant single-char string to `LastIndexOf(char)`. Benchmarks suggest this is nearly 2x faster (19.02ns -> 10.53ns)
- Consistency improvements to certain documentation comments.
- Replaced `Mathf.Max(rs.RFind("/"), rs.RFind("\\"));` with `rs.AsSpan().LastIndexOfAny('/', '\\');`. `AsSpan` must be used for performance since `LastIndexOfAny` on strings only take an array.
- Replaced `!= -1` with `< 0`, including the `from` parameter for `RFind`. This matches the C++ implementation.
- Replaced `a == b || a == c` with `a is b or c`, both for clarity and to fix a bug. `IsValidHexNumber` currently considers `-` valid but not `+`, due to a precedence bug with `||` and `&&`.
- Replaced custom local `IsHexDigit` function with `char.IsAsciiHexDigit`, both for simplicity and also because the current implementation uses `char.IsDigit` rather than `char.IsAsciiDigit`, which is presumably incorrect since it would accept non-ASCII numbers in the hex number like the Japanese １２３ full-width numerals.
- Replaced `IndexOfAny(...) == -1` with `!AsSpan().ContainsAny(...)` for clarity. I also changed the array to a `SearchValues` because C# was giving a warning to change to it for performance.
- Replaced `IsValidInt` + `ToInt` + bounds check with `byte.TryParse` and `ushort.TryParse` for simplicity and performance.
- Optimized `JSONEscape` by avoiding multiple passes. Benchmarks suggest this is nearly 5x faster (339.79ns -> 74.15ns, 384B -> 288B)
- Added `RFind` overload with `char` to match the `Find` overload with `char`. These could also be added to e.g. `RFindN` but you would have to add it to `FindN` as well.
- Replaced some seemingly pointless code in `ValidateNodeName` with something simpler and more performant.
